newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan budget debate resumes despite boycott.
newsitem.headline: Japan budget debate resumes despite boycott.

text.p: A key budget committee in the Lower House of Japan's parliament resumed debate on Wednesday despite a continued boycott by the three main opposition parties, a parliamentary official said.

The committee had been scheduled to convene from 9 a.m. (0000 GMT), but was unable to do so due to the absence of the three parties -- Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), the Democratic Party and the Taiyo (Sun) Party.

The parties are boycotting the proceedings because the ruling Liberal Democratic Party has refused to accept their demands for revisions to an extra budget for the current fiscal year, which ends on March 31, opposition sources said.
"We decided to proceed with the debate by asking parties other than the three to start their questions. We will continue to ask the boycotting parties to attend," the official said.
